Find your Air Show/Essex/Clacton-on-Sea

Clacton Airshow

A free seaside air show on the Essex coast

Clacton is one of the friendliest seaside shows in the calendar. Warbirds, fast jets and display teams over the North Sea, a pier full of rides just along the front, and in 2026 a twilight display on the Thursday evening. Here’s how I would plan your days by the sea.

WhenThursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027
EntryFree
ShowgroundWest Greensward, from 11:00 (2026)
StationClacton-on-Sea, about 15 min walk
2027 confirmedTendring District Council has confirmed Clacton Airshow for Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027. The line-up, flying times and travel details haven’t been announced yet, so those are based on the 2025 and 2026 shows for now.

The show at a glance

Clacton Airshow runs along the seafront either side of the pier, with the crowd centre on the West Greensward. Tendring District Council puts it on, it’s free to watch and 2026 was its 33rd year.

What I like about Clacton is that it’s held on a Thursday and Friday at the end of August, so it feels a little calmer than the big weekend seafront shows. The Airshow Village on the West Greensward opens at 11:00, and the flying fills the afternoon on both days.

The Thursday is the one to circle. After the afternoon display there’s a twilight display over the sea, with aerobatics, lit up aircraft and pyrotechnics against the seafront. If you can only make one day and you don’t mind a later finish, I would suggest the Thursday.

The main things to plan for are the seafront road closures and parking. I would advise using the Park and Ride or the train, and arriving well before the flying starts.

Meet the RAF

In 2026 the RAF Careers Engagement team brought a replica Typhoon cockpit and a Batak reaction challenge to the West Greensward. It’s a great way for your kids to learn about the different roles in the RAF, and if anyone in your group would like to join, it’s the place to ask any questions they may have.

At most UK shows the RAF display teams spend time on the ground too, like the Red Arrows pilots and their ground crew, where kids can get stickers and take photos. It’s worth keeping an eye out for them in the Airshow Village between displays.

    Our view

    If you can get a weekday off at the end of August, I would suggest Clacton. You get the Red Arrows and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight for free, a proper seaside town on your doorstep and, on the Thursday, a twilight display you won’t see at most shows. Use the Park and Ride or the train, arrive early and stay for the evening if you can.

    Ways to arrive

    Based on the 2025 and 2026 shows. Fares, times and parking for 2027 are still to be confirmed.

    Do I need a ticket?
    No. Watching from the seafront is free. The council asks for donations to help keep the show going, online through the official website or in the bucket collections, and the £6 programme helps too.
    Which roads close?
    Road closures and temporary traffic measures are put in place around the seafront. The council hasn’t published the exact roads, so follow the signs and stewards on the day, allow extra time and don’t rely on parking on the seafront.
    How does the Park and Ride work?
    You park at Clacton Shopping Village on Stephenson Road West and take the bus to the seafront. In 2025 buses ran about every 10 minutes from 10:00, with return fares of £5 adult, £4 child (5 to 19) or £15 for a group of up to five. The last bus back left the seafront at 22:00 on the Thursday and 18:30 on the Friday.
    Where do coaches go?
    Coaches drop off at Angle Field, CO15 6PH. In 2026 the advised route was Wash Lane, Freeland Road, Tower Road, Marine Parade and Marine Parade East to Angle Field, then on to Clacton Leisure Centre, Vista Road, CO15 6DB, to park.
    Can I camp on the seafront?
    No. A High Court injunction stops unauthorised camping in the designated seafront areas around the show. In 2026 it ran from Thursday 20 August to Saturday 5 September. The campsites and holiday parks in the Where to stay section are the way to go.
    Will I get home after the twilight display?
    On the Thursday the flying carries on into the evening. In 2025 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00. If you’re on the train, check the last train back before you set off, and I would advise leaving a little before the very end if your connection is tight.

    Where to stay

    Clacton is a seaside town with hotels, guest houses and plenty of holiday parks within a few miles of the seafront. The show is at the end of the summer holidays, so I would advise booking as early as you can.

    Help On Show Days

    Clacton is a relaxed show, but it’s still a busy seafront with thousands of people, a twilight display and road closures to think about. Here’s what to do if something goes wrong, plus quick answers to the questions I see asked most before the show.

    In an emergency, call 999. For anything else on the day, find the nearest steward or head to the Airshow Village on the West Greensward.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    Lost Each Other

    Agree a meeting point as soon as you arrive, like the entrance to the pier or the West Greensward toilets. For younger children, I would advise writing your phone number on their wrist. If you can’t find them, tell a steward straight away.

    Feeling Unwell

    Tell the nearest steward and they can get help to you. On West Beach the lifeguards give first aid while they’re on duty. There’s very little shade on the seafront, so drink plenty.

    Flying Times

    The times are in the official programme, sold on the West Greensward. Timings can change for operational reasons or the weather, so keep an eye on the official social media.

    Away From The Commentary

    If you’re watching from Martello Bay or the pier, Radio Airshow on Actual Radio carried the commentary in 2026. More in .

    Bad Weather

    Sea mist, low cloud or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. The cafés and the pier are your best shelter while it passes.

    Loud Displays

    The council warns that some displays are very noisy and may upset people who are sensitive to noise. I would advise ear defenders for children.

    Getting Home

    In 2025 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00 on the Thursday and 18:30 on the Friday. Check yours, and your last train, before the twilight display. See .

    Finding Your Car

    After the twilight display it’s dark and everyone leaves at once. Drop a pin on your phone’s map when you park, it saves a lot of wandering.

    Quick Answers

    Is it free?

    Yes, it’s free to watch from the seafront. Donations online, in the bucket collections or by buying the programme help keep it that way.

    When is it in 2027?

    Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August 2027, on Clacton seafront.

    What time does it start?

    In 2026 the Airshow Village on the West Greensward opened at 11:00, with the flying through the afternoon on both days. The 2027 times come out nearer the show.

    Is there a twilight display in 2027?

    There was one on the Thursday evening in 2026, but it hasn’t been confirmed for 2027 yet. I would advise keeping an eye on the official site.

    How much is the programme?

    It was £6 in 2026, sold on the West Greensward. It has the flight times and facts about the aircraft.

    Can I bring my dog?

    Dogs aren’t allowed on West Beach from May to September, except guide dogs. On the promenade they need to be on a lead. With the noise, I would think hard about whether your dog will enjoy it.

    Can I have a BBQ on the beach?

    No. Gas barbecues aren’t allowed on West Beach.

    Can I fly my drone?

    No, unauthorised drones aren’t allowed at the event.

    Can I camp on the seafront?

    No. A court injunction stops unauthorised camping on the seafront around the show. See for campsites nearby.

    Where are the toilets?

    The West Greensward toilets are on Marine Parade Way, with a Changing Places toilet next door. There are also toilets at Pier Gap. More in .

    Are there lifeguards?

    West Beach has lifeguards in the school holidays and at weekends, from 10:30 to 17:30.

    Can I go for a swim?

    The council doesn’t advise swimming at West Beach, because of the water quality and the groynes and pier. I would stick to paddling.

    I don’t have an answer for that here. The official Clacton Airshow site may help.

      Quieter, with more room to spread out a tripod or a monopod. Light: aircraft turning at this end are often backlit in the afternoon, so I would suggest it more for the morning arrivals and practice passes.

    Tides And The Beach

    West Beach is golden sand, running from Groyne 41 to the pier, below the West Greensward. Around low tide there’s plenty of room between the groynes. Around high tide the sea comes much further up, and the beach gets a lot narrower. If you want to sit on the sand, I would advise checking the tide before you set up.

    West Beach

    LifeguardsSchool holidays and weekends, 10:30 to 17:30
    SwimmingNot advised by the council
    DogsNone, May to September
    GroundSand, with groynes

    Beach Space Through The Flying

    Loading the latest tide forecast for Clacton.

    Set up above the line

    Look for the line of seaweed and damp sand. That’s roughly where the last high tide reached, so pitch above it if the tide is coming in.

    Mind the groynes

    The wooden groynes split the beach into bays. When the tide comes in, a bay can fill quickly, so keep your bags together and know your way back up to the prom.

    Paddling, not swimming

    The council flags West Beach as not advised for swimming, because of the water quality and the dangers around the groynes and the pier. I would stick to a paddle.

    Dogs on the beach

    From May to September dogs aren’t allowed on West Beach, except guide dogs. On the promenade they need to be on a lead.

    Sea Mist And Wind

    A seafront show has its own weather. It can be bright and sunny in town while a bank of mist sits out over the North Sea, right where the aircraft fly. It’s worth knowing what to look out for, so a grey morning doesn’t put you off.

    Who Decides?

    Fly or notThe display teams and organisers
    WhenOn the day, display by display
    Latest newsThe official social media
    Why mist forms

    When warm, damp air drifts over the cooler sea, it cools down and turns into mist or fog. It often sits just off the coast while the town stays sunny.

    It can lift quickly

    A misty morning doesn’t always mean a misty afternoon. As the day warms up, the mist often thins or drifts away, so I would suggest staying put rather than giving up early.

    Lower cloud, different show

    Teams like the Red Arrows fly a full looping display when the cloud is high, and a rolling or flat display when it’s lower. You’ll still see them, just a different routine.

    The wind off the sea

    Strong or gusty wind can stop some displays, especially lighter historic aircraft. It also makes the beach feel much colder, and it gets cooler still for the twilight display, so bring layers.

    Jack’s tipOn a misty day, keep an eye on the official social media for any changes, and look out to sea rather than at the sky above you. The mist is often worse over the water than over the town.

    This is a general guide, not an official forecast. For the live weather and a flying conditions check, see .

    Along The Seafront

    Most people watch from the West Greensward or the beach below it, but the show is visible right along the front. Moving away from the crowd centre gives you a very different day, so think about who you’re with and how close you want to be.

    Shooting at Clacton

    The crowd looks out to sea, roughly south south east, so you’re shooting into the sun around the middle of the day and it swings round to your right through the afternoon. By the Thursday twilight display the sun has set behind your right shoulder. Aircraft fly further out than at an airfield, so reach matters more here.

Flying times change each day, so check the official programme on the day. Cloud and sea haze will soften everything shown here. The seafront is redrawn as a guide and is not to scale, so treat distances as approximate.

    Get creative over the sea

    Clacton has its challenges for photographers. The crowd line faces out to sea and towards the sun for much of the day, so aircraft can look dark against a bright sky, and sea haze can soften detail and flatten the colour. I would suggest using the sun guide to plan when you shoot, adding a little exposure compensation when you are shooting into the sun, and saving your close up work for later in the afternoon, when the light swings round behind you.

    Ideas to try

    • Wait for the banking passes. A topside or underside view shows far more of the aircraft than a straight flypast.
    • Leave room in the frame for smoke trails, so they lead the eye to the aircraft.
    • Zoom out now and then to include the pier, the beach or the crowds on the Greensward, so the photo says Clacton.
    • On the Thursday evening, try a slower shutter for the twilight display, so the aircraft lights and pyrotechnics leave trails.

    Starting settings

    Pick what’s flying and the weather for a starting point. It never goes faster than 1/2000 or above ISO 1200, so the files stay clean and the shutter stays realistic for the subject. Check your histogram after the first pass and adjust.

    Making The Day Easier

    It’s free

    No tickets to buy for the kids. The programme and parking are the only things you need to pay for.

    Ear defenders

    The council warns some displays are very loud. I would advise ear defenders for babies and toddlers, especially for the fast jets.

    The pier

    Rides, arcades and food just east of the show. A good place to fill the time before the flying starts.

    Sun and shade

    There’s very little shade on the seafront. Pack sun cream, hats and plenty of water.

    Bucket and spade

    West Beach is golden sand, so a bucket and spade keeps little ones busy between displays.

    Toilets

    The West Greensward toilets and the Changing Places toilet are close by. See .

    Jack’s tipIf you’re staying for the twilight display, I would suggest bringing a warm top and a torch for the walk back. Little ones will be tired, so plan where you’re heading before it gets dark.

    Food, toilets & access

    Clacton has a real advantage over airfield shows: a whole town sits right behind the display line. Eat in the Airshow Village, bring a picnic, or step back into town for a sit down meal.

    Food & drink

    Traders and food stalls in the Airshow Village on the West Greensward, plus the cafés, chip shops and pubs in town and on the pier. Queues peak around lunchtime, so eat a little earlier or later.

    Kids’ activities

    The RAF careers team, hands-on and STEM activities in the village, the beach, and the rides and arcades on the pier.

    Toilets

    The West Greensward public toilets are on Marine Parade Way, CO15 1ND, with accessible toilets, baby changing and a Changing Places toilet next door. Go before the flying starts.

    The beach

    The beach below the Greensward is sand, split up by groynes. Check the tide times before you set up on it, as high tide leaves far less room.

    Accessibility
    The promenade and the Greensward are the easiest places to watch from with a wheelchair or pushchair, as the sand is hard going. The Changing Places toilet next to the West Greensward toilets has a hoist, bed and shower, and you need to apply for an Access Key to use it. The council hasn’t published an accessible viewing area or Blue Badge parking for the show, so I would advise calling Tendring District Council on 01255 686868 before you travel.
    Blue Badge parking
    The town car parks have disabled bays, including 12 at Carnarvon Road and 6 at Wellesley Road, and at the time of checking Blue Badge holders could park free for up to three hours at Wellesley Road. Seafront car parks near the display are often closed during the show. Spaces are first come, first served, so I would advise arriving early and checking the council’s car parking page before you go.
    Noise
    The council warns that some displays are particularly noisy and may distress people who are sensitive to noise. Ear defenders are well worth bringing for children.
    Drones
    Unauthorised drones aren’t permitted at the event.
    Programme
    The official programme, with flight times and facts about the aircraft, was £6 in 2026, sold at the West Greensward Airshow site. Buying one helps fund the free show.
    Supporting the show
    Clacton Airshow is free to watch but costs a lot to put on. The council asks for donations online through the official website or in the bucket collections, and encourages visitors to bring some cash on the day.
    Listen live
    In 2026 Radio Airshow was broadcast on Actual Radio across both days. Ask a smart speaker to play Radio Airshow, or use the Actual Radio app or website. It’s handy for the commentary if you’re away from the crowd centre.
    If the weather turns
    Sea mist, low cloud or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. Timings can change for operational reasons or the weather, so check the official channels on the morning and pack a waterproof.

    • Comfort

    • Low chairs or a blanket
    • Sun cream & hat
    • A warm layer for the evening

    • Family

    • Ear defenders
    • Picnic & water
    • Some cash for the programme and buckets

    • Camera

    • The longest lens you have
    • Lens cloth for sea spray
    • Spare batteries & cards
